summary: Trajan is a dense Feld point-salad game where the mancala-like bowl mechanism constrains which of six actions you can take each turn, forcing you to plan several moves ahead to line up the action you actually need. Turns are quick once you know the system, but the puzzle of managing your tableau and reading opponents' bowls to avoid being blocked is the whole game.
praised: Tight, puzzly turn planning with meaningful long-term sequencing
Multiple viable strategies and good replayability
Efficient turns once the system clicks
criticised: Steep learning curve and unintuitive rules explanation
Point-salad scoring can feel like an accounting exercise
Low direct interaction; can feel like parallel solitaire

interaction.kind: mostly parallel play with some indirect blocking via forum tile drafting and senate track positioning

scoring.why: Points trickle in from building, trading, military campaigns, senate influence, and forum tile sets, so the winner is whoever chains the bowl-action system most efficiently across several tracks rather than dominating one.
